article_title: Alternative AI Philosophy: Daoism as Method for AI in Education
citation: Qin Xie. (2026). Alternative AI Philosophy: Daoism as Method for AI in Education.
title: The Zhenren (真人) as a new myth or learner ideal for AI in education
description: The Zhenren, one who has fully realized the Dao, is proposed as a counter-ideal to the passive, algorithmically managed learner. As the Zhuangzi states, "only when there is a Zhenren can there be true knowledge." The Zhenren is a natural learner who treats AI only as an intellectual prosthesis, rejects both technological fanaticism and technophobia, and interrogates algorithmic taxonomies that sort learners into fixed categories. The ideal functions as "a replicable soteriological program rather than an elitist fantasy," democratically available to every learner, and reimagines learning as "the harmonious integration of self, society, and cosmos" rather than data-driven efficiency.
requirements: Disciplined practice through which learners cultivate innate nature and relational embeddedness; first-person experiential labor with AI as prosthesis only
constraints: The article notes scholars diverge on interpreting the ideal, e.g., Ames's processual "Authentic Person" reading versus Campany's soteriological-program framework
target_learners: every learner, regardless of background, gender, or class
target_learning_goals: achieving equanimity, spontaneity, and cosmological unity; remaining cognitively present and ethically accountable
examples: The article positions the Zhenren against algorithmic management tools such as IMPACT, TVAAS, and EVAAS, which it says can fail to respect individual agency
key_sources: Qin Xie. (2026). Alternative AI Philosophy: Daoism as Method for AI in Education. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10842

article_title: An Investigation into the Impact of Reflective Teaching on EFL Learners' Autonomy and Intrinsic Motivation
citation: Abdolrezapour, P., & Fallah, E. (2015). An investigation into the impact of reflective teaching on EFL learners’ autonomy and intrinsic motivation. Cypriot Journal of Educational Science. 10(4), 305-315. https://doi.org/10.18844/cjes.v10i4.229
title: Zhang and Li (2004) learner autonomy questionnaire
description: A 21-item questionnaire developed by Zhang and Li (2004) used to measure participants' autonomy. "The first 11 items form the fir st part", answered with frequency options from never to always, and the remaining 10 items form a second part with five choices per item. Piloted on 30 similar students, it showed a Cronbach Alpha of 0.741 in this study.
requirements: Two-part format: 11 frequency-scale items plus 10 five-choice items
examples: Administered before and after treatment to both groups to check homogeneity and measure change
key_sources: Abdolrezapour, P., & Fallah, E. (2015). An investigation into the impact of reflective teaching on EFL learners’ autonomy and intrinsic motivation. Cypriot Journal of Educational Science. 10(4), 305-315. https://doi.org/10.18844/cjes.v10i4.229
